mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which signals economic strength and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is low but SPX returns are negative, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) drops below 0.25%, it indicates monetary easing, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS drops below 0.25% but SPX returns are negative, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) together indicate strong demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both RSAFS and HOUST rise but SPX returns are negative, this hypothesis is refuted.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, rising FEDFUNDS leads to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises in a tightening cycle but SPX returns are positive, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases but SPX returns are negative, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) above 3% indicates strong demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth exceeds 3% but SPX returns are negative, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (RSAFS) together indicate a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both PAYEMS and RSAFS rise but SPX returns are negative, this hypothesis is refuted.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment (UNRATE) below 7% leads to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is below 7% in late-cycle but SPX returns are negative, this hypothesis fails.
